title: Nana Asma'u
tagline: The girl who learned the Qur'an by heart, and grew up to teach a whole land: the woman this site is named after.
depictionNotes: Nana Asma'u (about 1793 to 1864), her father the Shehu Usman dan Fodio and the people around her are shown, all with dark skin. The Prophet ﷺ is mentioned and never shown; Asma bint Abi Bakr, a Companion, is shown only from behind and by her hands. The pictures are AI-generated (Google Gemini), drawn from approved character designs so that people look the same from scene to scene. The facts come from Boyd and Mack's Collected Works of Nana Asma'u (1997) and other named sources; the war years and the captives are not told to children, and each chapter's note for parents says so.
coverAlt: Nana Asma'u reading to a circle of women and girls in a Sokoto courtyard, with two teachers in tall straw hats.
